meanings.note: Warm, natural Levantine greeting usable at any time of day.
Placed before a name or title whenever addressing someone directly (يا دينا، يا مس فاتن); natural English usually drops it.
Singular بنت, definite البنت, plural بنات / البنات ('AlRawabi School for Girls' = مدرسة الروابي للبنات).

examples.trans: She is a very bright girl.
The girls are standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Versatile Levantine word meaning 'but' between clauses and 'only / just' inside a clause.
As a focus adverb before a verb, noun, or imperative, بس narrows or softens the statement.

examples.trans: I tried to speak, but she didn't hear me.

meanings.note: Often used as a cognate object with سأل (سألتك سؤال 'she asked you a question').
After a noun, means 'one' (إشي واحد، سؤال واحد، إيد واحدة); with الـ (الواحد) it is the everyday impersonal subject 'a person / one'.

examples.trans: A person has to tell the truth.

meanings.note: Asks about manner or state (كيف كان الفيلم؟ 'how was the movie?', شفت كيف... 'I saw how...').
Two essential senses: 'happen' (اللي صار 'what happened') and 'become / turn into' (صارت كابوس، صار الوقت).

examples.trans: It's time we head to class.

meanings.note: Takes suffixes معي (with me), معك (with you), معها (with her), معنا (with us), معكم (with you all), معهم (with them), and forms مع السلامة! ('Goodbye!').
Placed before a definite noun without changing form: بنفس الغرفة ('in the same room'), بنفس الوقت ('at the same time').

examples.trans: We arrived at the same time.

meanings.note: Singular غرفة (الغرفة), plural غرف (تقسيم الغرف 'room assignments').

examples.trans: We are in the same room on the trip.
The room is neat and spacious.

meanings.note: Construes with على for answering a person (ردي عليها 'answer her!').
Takes pronoun endings: علي (on/about me), عليكي (to you, f.), عليها (to her), علينا (on/for us), عليكم (on you, pl.). Often contracts to عـ before الـ.

examples.trans: Count on me in this matter.
They lied about me in front of the teacher.

meanings.note: Takes the person asked directly (اسألي البنت، سألتك سؤال).

examples.trans: I want to ask you a simple question.
Ask the teacher about the homework.

meanings.note: Form II verb (battal) used in imperatives like بطلي حركاتك ('cut out your antics').
In the plural حركات, often means 'attitude / games / antics' (بطلي حركاتك الباردة).

examples.trans: I noticed every move she made.

meanings.note: Describes chilly weather or an unbothered, icy attitude (حركاتك الباردة).

examples.trans: The weather is a bit cold today.
She replied to me in a cold way.

meanings.note: In the set phrase على فكرة, introduces a side remark: 'by the way / for your information'.

examples.trans: I have a nice idea for the trip.

examples.text: على فكرة، أنا سمعت كل إشي.
examples.trans: By the way, I heard everything.

meanings.note: Independent first-person singular pronoun for any gender.

examples.trans: I am a student at the school.

meanings.note: Levantine pronunciation of مثل (mitil); متلكم تماماً means 'just like you'.

examples.trans: There is no school like ours.

meanings.note: Intensifies similarity or agreement: متلكم تماماً ('just like you').

examples.trans: I know exactly what you mean.

meanings.note: Negates nouns, adjectives, participles, prepositional phrases, and لازم (مش صح، مش معنا، مش قادرة، مش بعد اليوم).
Signature Levantine word (pronounced ktiir) used before or after adjectives ('very') and after plural nouns ('many').

examples.trans: I have lots of friends at school.

meanings.note: The everyday Jordanian word for 'happy / pleased' (مش كتير مبسوطة 'not very thrilled').
Everyday Jordanian masculine demonstrative used before a definite noun (هاد الإشي، هاد الحكي) or as a pronoun (حتى لو هاد آخر إشي).
هاد الوضع refers to an awkward or tense arrangement.

examples.trans: The situation at school is tense today.
I'm not comfortable with this situation.

meanings.note: Imperative forms with object pronouns give خليكم بحالكم ('stay in your own business') and خلوني بحالي ('leave me in mine').

examples.trans: Let me speak for a bit.

meanings.note: With suffixes, acts as the Levantine reflexive ('myself/themselves': حالهم), 'alone' (لحالك), and 'one's own business' (خليكم بحالكم).

examples.trans: I studied the lesson by myself.

meanings.note: Used in conversational questions like تفتكري سمعت كل إشي؟ ('do you think she heard everything?').

examples.trans: Do you think she'll come today?
I thought you were in class.

meanings.note: Imperative feminine اسمعي منيح ('listen closely'); past سمعت ('she heard / I heard').

examples.trans: Listen to what I want to tell you.
I heard every word they said.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun, كل means 'every' (كل يوم، كل إشي); with الـ (الكل) it means 'everyone'; with suffixes (كلنا، كلهم، كلها) 'all of us/them/it'.

examples.trans: We see each other every day.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian word corresponding to formal شيء; definite form الإشي, plural أشياء.

examples.trans: There is something important I want to say.

meanings.note: Core Levantine question word for 'what?' (شو صار؟) and casual conversation starter ('So, ...').
With pronoun suffixes: ما كان قصدي ('I didn't mean to') and شو قصدك؟ ('what do you mean?').

examples.trans: I swear I didn't mean to upset you.
What do you mean by this question?

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun, أي asks 'which?' (أي موضوع؟) or strengthens negation ('not any' -> أي إشي).
Used for an issue under discussion (هاد الموضوع، أي موضوع بالضبط؟).

examples.trans: The matter is more serious than I thought.

meanings.note: Appears in the everyday adverbial phrase بالضبط (pronounced biz-zabt in Jordan), meaning 'exactly'.

examples.trans: That is exactly what I mean.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of حكى; هاد الحكي means 'this talk / this claim'.

examples.trans: I heard all the talk that happened.

meanings.note: Invariable Levantine relative pronoun replacing الذي / التي / الذين and 'what' (اللي صار 'what happened').

examples.trans: The girl whom I saw is my friend.

meanings.note: At school, الحمام refers to the student washroom/restroom.

examples.trans: I went to the washroom during recess.

meanings.note: Negates past and b-present verbs (ما إجيت، ما بعرف) and idioms like ما عليكم ('never mind'); after قبل or بدل (قبل ما، بدل ما) it links a verb clause.
In the past مع ما (ما عرفت شو أعمل), means 'I didn't know what to do'; b-present بعرف means 'I know'.

examples.trans: I didn't know how to answer the question.

meanings.note: High-frequency Jordanian discourse word meaning 'okay, settled!' or 'drop it / enough!'.
Imperative feminine اسكتي ('be quiet!'); ما رح نسكت means 'we won't stay silent'.

examples.trans: Everyone fell silent when the principal entered.
We won't stay quiet about our right.

meanings.note: High-frequency Levantine word for 'now' (contracted from هاد الوقت).

examples.trans: We have to go to class right now.
I feel a bit relieved now.

meanings.note: Appears in the classic Arabic farewell مع السلامة! ('Goodbye!', literally 'with safety').
